newsitem.title: USA: Most US governors oppose cap on Medicaid spending.
newsitem.headline: Most US governors oppose cap on Medicaid spending.

text.p: U.S. state governors on Monday urged White House and Congressional budget negotiators not to cap spending on the Medicaid health care program.

"We adamantly oppose a cap on federal Medicaid spending in any form," National Governors Association Chairman Bob Miller of Nevada and 39 other governors said in a letter to President Bill Clinton and to Republican and Democratic leaders in Congress.
"Unilateral caps in Medicaid spending will result in cost shifts to states, enabling the federal government to balance its budget at the expense of the states," the letter said.

They said the level of Medicaid savings should be kept at $8 billion, saying governors had already contributed to budget deficit reduction by restraining Medicaid spending significantly in recent years.
